title: One map instead of two
body: The old flat map has been removed; everything now draws on the 3D map, which still opens looking straight down. One map engine to load, and no more features that only exist on one of them.

title: The map is the 3D one now, lying flat
body: The tool now opens on the 3D map, looking straight down. It tilts once an estimate is ready.

title: Relief slider moved off the map
body: The relief slider sat on top of the map it was adjusting. It now lives in the controls card.

title: Tilt the 3D view all the way to the horizon
body: The 3D view now tilts to a near-horizon angle, which is what shows you a blocking ridge.

title: The 3D view finally has hills in it
body: The 3D view now shows real elevation, exaggerated six times so Dutch relief is visible, and says by how much.

title: Pick between same-prefix repeaters on the map
body: Two repeaters can share a prefix. Resolve on map shows the one the tool did not pick; click to swap it in, then Apply.

title: Sharper estimates from a softer idea of coverage
body: Coverage now fades with distance instead of stopping at an edge. Typical miss drops from 2.9 km to 2.4 km.

title: Places the height data cannot see no longer win by default
body: Spots the height data cannot see no longer beat spots it checked and found blocked. Inland, nothing changes.

title: Cluster cards are readable again
body: The step 2 cluster cards were green-on-green and barely readable. They are now dark tiles with a green edge on the one you picked.

title: Better line-of-sight checks, and honesty about the gaps
body: Line of sight now uses proper diffraction maths and the earth's curve, and says so when the height data does not reach.

title: Says when a duplicate repeater was picked by guesswork
body: Where no proven link decides between two same-prefix repeaters, the tool guesses the nearest one and now says how often.

title: Estimates no longer look more precise than they are
body: Positions were printed to the metre but land a median 2 km out. Now three decimals, with the typical error beside them.

title: Coverage now based on what a repeater can hear
body: Coverage counted outbound-only links, which run longer and made it too generous. It now prefers inbound evidence.

title: Ignoring impossible repeater links
body: Links too long to be a single hop are now ignored, and the tool says how many.

title: Sharper estimates from overlapping observers
body: Observers are now combined by where they all agree, rather than letting the loudest outvote the geometry.

title: Range and confidence outlines drawn correctly
body: The shaded outlines around ranges, clusters and the estimate were collapsing to a line. Fixed.

title: Repeater lookups working again
body: Prefix searches had stopped reaching MC Radar and were falling back to a thinner source. Fixed.

title: A short guide for newcomers
body: First-time visitors now get a walkthrough of the three steps and the tuning controls. Reopen it anytime with the ? button.

title: Share a link to your search
body: A Share button copies a link to your current clues, so you can hand someone the exact search instead of describing it.

title: Cleaner map controls
body: Buttons no longer float on top of the map. Clear Map and the 3D toggle now sit together above Step 1.

title: Shareable links
body: Step 1 can now be pre-filled from a URL, so other sites can link straight into a result instead of a blank form.

title: Smarter clustering
body: Repeaters heard through a relay (2nd-hop) are now included based on real network links where available, not just a flat guessed range.

title: Duplicate-node fix
body: Switching between duplicate nodes for the same prefix no longer silently resets the weight you'd set.

title: New top bar
body: Added a Dutch MeshCore-branded top bar with links to the community site, Mesh-Hunter, MC-Radar, and this project's GitHub.

title: Tighter default search radius
body: Cluster search radius now defaults to 6km instead of 50km, matching typical real-world repeater density.

title: Docker deploy
body: One-command deploy via Docker Compose with a built-in Cloudflare Tunnel sidecar.
